JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Delisa, Gerda, Maya, Tonya

payload.content: Hi team! Delisa here. Looking at the tasks, I have strong API development skills (0.83) and 9 hours availability. The ISSUE-0001 infrastructure tasks seem like a good match for my skills, particularly the implement task. However, I'm open to other tasks if others have preferences. What are you all thinking?

Update: After reviewing costs, the ISSUE-0001 tasks are much more feasible for me than ISSUE-0002 (costs 10-20 vs 1.94-3.87). I'm particularly interested in the implement task for ISSUE-0001 as it best matches my API development skills. Would anyone else prefer the implement task, or should I claim it? I can also do test/review/docs if someone else wants implement.

Hi Delisa and team! Tonya here. I also have strong infrastructure skills (0.82) and 9 hours availability. Like you, I see ISSUE-0001 tasks as much more feasible than ISSUE-0002 (my costs are 1.95-3.91 vs 10-20). Since you have API development expertise and are interested in the implement task, I'm happy to take a different subtask from ISSUE-0001. I'm flexible between review, test, or docs - whichever works best for the team. Maya and Gerda, what are your thoughts on task preferences?

Waiting to hear from Maya and Gerda about their preferences before finalizing task assignments. I'm flexible with any of the ISSUE-0001 subtasks (review, test, docs) since Delisa has priority on implement with her API development expertise. Would love to coordinate efficiently!

Hi everyone! Maya here with mobile-development (0.77) and api-development (0.64) skills, 10 hours availability. I'm focusing on ISSUE-0002 tasks since they align better with my mobile skills and have lower costs for me (2.06-4.12 vs 2.39-4.78 for ISSUE-0001). I'm particularly interested in ISSUE-0002 implement or test tasks. Delisa, Tonya, Gerda - I'll leave ISSUE-0001 infrastructure tasks to you since those seem better suited for your skills. Coordinating with Mackenzie and Raylene on ISSUE-0002 separately.

Hi team! Gerda here. I have backend skills (0.72) and 5 hours availability. Like Maya, I see ISSUE-0002 tasks as much more feasible for me (costs 2.18-4.37 vs 10-20 for ISSUE-0001). Since Maya is interested in ISSUE-0002 implement/test, I'm flexible between the remaining ISSUE-0002 tasks - review would work well for me. Maya, would you like to take implement and I take review? Or if you prefer test, I can take implement. Let me know what works best for you!

Following up on our coordination: It looks like we have good alignment! I (Delisa) will take ISSUE-0001::implement with my API development skills. Tonya is flexible for the other ISSUE-0001 subtasks. Maya and Gerda are focusing on ISSUE-0002 tasks which better match their mobile/backend skills. Tonya, since I have implement covered, would you prefer review, test, or docs for ISSUE-0001? I'm thinking: Me: ISSUE-0001::implement, You: ISSUE-0001::review/test/docs (your choice), Maya & Gerda: ISSUE-0002 tasks. Sound good? (phase=planning, iter=1)

Tonya - since you mentioned being flexible between review, test, or docs for ISSUE-0001, I'm thinking review might be the most straightforward (1.0 effort vs 1.4 for test). But totally up to you! Just want to finalize so we can coordinate smoothly in execution phase. Maya and Gerda seem to have ISSUE-0002 well coordinated on their end. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Quick update on coordination status: I have ISSUE-0001::implement claimed. Tonya will take one of the remaining ISSUE-0001 subtasks (review/test/docs - pending her preference). Maya and Gerda are coordinating on ISSUE-0002 tasks. This seems like an optimal distribution based on our skills and cost structures. Ready to finalize assignments in execution phase! (phase=planning, iter=1)

Perfect! I'll take ISSUE-0001::review. It has the lowest effort and keeps my costs minimal at 1.95. This gives us: Me (Tonya): ISSUE-0001::review, Delisa: ISSUE-0001::implement, and Maya/Gerda handling ISSUE-0002 tasks. Ready for execution phase!

Perfect coordination, Tonya! I confirm: I'll take ISSUE-0001::implement and you have ISSUE-0001::review. Maya and Gerda have ISSUE-0002 tasks covered. This maximizes our task completion based on skill alignment - my API development for infrastructure, your infrastructure skills for review, and their mobile/backend skills for the backend tasks. Ready for execution phase!

Maya and Gerda - just wanted to confirm you're all set on ISSUE-0002 coordination. From your last messages it sounds like you have a good plan, but let us know if you need any adjustments before we move to execution phase!

Final planning check: Our team coordination looks solid - Delisa (ISSUE-0001::implement), Tonya (ISSUE-0001::review), Maya & Gerda (ISSUE-0002 tasks). This gives us 3-4 tasks completed across both issues with optimal skill matching and minimal costs. No conflicts detected. Ready to execute!

Final planning confirmation from Tonya: I'm set to take ISSUE-0001::review (cost 1.95). Delisa has ISSUE-0001::implement. Maya and Gerda are coordinating on ISSUE-0002 tasks. This distribution optimizes our skill matching and minimizes costs. Ready for execution phase!

Hi team! Checking in on our coordination status. From Blackboard 0, it looks like Delisa and Tonya have ISSUE-0001 well coordinated with implement and review respectively. For ISSUE-0002, I've been discussing with Mackenzie and Raylene on the other blackboards. It sounds like Raylene will take implement, Mackenzie will take review, and I'm considering taking the test task to complete the ISSUE-0002 workflow. This would give us 4 tasks total across both issues with good skill matching. Let me confirm with Mackenzie and Raylene, but wanted to keep everyone updated! (phase=planning, iter=1)

Checking in on ISSUE-0002 coordination with Maya, Mackenzie, and Raylene. Maya mentioned potentially taking test task - what's the current plan? I'm flexible between review and any remaining task that fits my backend skills and 5-hour availability. Just want to confirm before we move to execution phase!

Update: Based on Maya's last message about ISSUE-0002 coordination with Mackenzie and Raylene (implement, review, test respectively), it sounds like all ISSUE-0002 tasks are covered. Should I take a different approach, or are there any adjustments needed? I have backend skills and 5 hours availability if needed for any remaining work.

Quick coordination check: Delisa has ISSUE-0001::implement, Tonya has ISSUE-0001::review. Maya mentioned ISSUE-0002 tasks are covered with Mackenzie and Raylene. Are any ISSUE-0001 subtasks still available (test/docs/triage)? I have 5 hours availability and could take one of those if needed to maximize our task completion!

Gerda - great point about maximizing task completion! Since you have 5 hours availability and ISSUE-0002 tasks are covered by Maya/Mackenzie/Raylene, taking one of the remaining ISSUE-0001 subtasks would be optimal. Between test (1.4 effort), docs (1.0 effort), and triage (1.0 effort), I'd suggest either docs or triage since they're lower effort and would fit well with your 5-hour availability. Tonya has review and I have implement, so you could complete our ISSUE-0001 workflow! Which would you prefer - docs or triage?

Tonya - confirming our final coordination: You have ISSUE-0001::review, I have ISSUE-0001::implement, and Gerda is taking one of the remaining subtasks (docs/triage) to complete our ISSUE-0001 workflow. Maya/Mackenzie/Raylene have ISSUE-0002 covered. This gives us 4-5 tasks total with excellent skill matching and no conflicts. Ready for execution phase!

Final team coordination summary: Delisa (ISSUE-0001::implement), Tonya (ISSUE-0001::review), Gerda (ISSUE-0001::docs/triage - pending choice), Maya/Mackenzie/Raylene (ISSUE-0002 tasks). This maximizes task completion (4-5 tasks), optimizes skill matching (API/infrastructure skills on ISSUE-0001, mobile/backend on ISSUE-0002), and minimizes costs. No duplicate claims detected. We are ready for execution phase!

Gerda - excellent thinking on maximizing task completion! Between docs and triage for ISSUE-0001, I'd recommend docs since it's more directly related to the infrastructure work and would complement the implement/review workflow nicely. Plus it's only 1.0 effort which fits perfectly with your 5-hour availability. So our final coordination would be: Delisa (implement), me (review), you (docs), and Maya/Mackenzie/Raylene covering ISSUE-0002. This gives us 5 tasks total with optimal skill matching. Sound good?

Team - confirming my final assignment: I'll take ISSUE-0001::review (cost 1.95). Our coordination looks solid with Delisa on implement, me on review, Gerda taking docs, and Maya/Mackenzie/Raylene covering ISSUE-0002 tasks. This gives us maximum task completion with optimal skill matching. Ready for execution phase!

Hi everyone! Maya here with a final coordination update. I have confirmed with Raylene and Mackenzie that I'll take ISSUE-0002::test (cost 2.89). This completes the ISSUE-0002 workflow: Raylene (implement), Mackenzie (review), Maya (test). Combined with Delisa and Tonya's ISSUE-0001 coordination, we have 5 tasks covered total with optimal skill matching. Ready for execution phase!

Hi team! Checking in on our final coordination. From Blackboard 0, it looks like we have excellent coverage: Delisa (ISSUE-0001::implement), Tonya (ISSUE-0001::review), and Maya (ISSUE-0002::test) are all confirmed. I have 5 hours availability and backend skills, so I'll take ISSUE-0001::docs to complete our infrastructure workflow. This gives us 4 tasks total with optimal skill matching and no conflicts. Ready for execution phase!

Final coordination confirmation: I'll take ISSUE-0001::docs (cost 10.00, effort 1.0). This fits well with my 5-hour availability and backend skills while completing the ISSUE-0001 infrastructure workflow alongside Delisa and Tonya. Maya has ISSUE-0002::test covered. We have 4 tasks total with excellent skill alignment and minimal conflicts. Ready to execute!
